content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper finetunes the pre-trained encoder to better matches the visual styles and preserve more content features. The finetuning is driven by a style contrastive loss and a content contrastive loss as well as a feature regularization loss. The new encoder can measure the style distance between different style images that better matches human perception.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths:**
+ The observation of the fact the pre-trained VGG fails to measure the style distance as humans is insightful. Thus, the motivation to solve this problem is clear. 
+ Idea to use contrastive learning to improve the feature extraction is intuitive and effective. The experiment in Fig. 1 and Fig. 10 shows that the trained encoder can better measure the style distance. 

**Weaknesses:**
+ The idea of using contrastive learning to improve the feature extraction is not new. The proposed content contrastive loss is similar to that in CUT Park et al. (2020). The style contrastive loss is similar to the Fixpoint triplet loss. The way of data augmentation is to model the style of an images with local patches, which is common in style transfer. The contrastive learning part looks less novel to me.
+ My main concern is the insignificant visual improvement. For example. In Fig. 4, the authors claim that ``In contrast, our results retain more content and are more style-consistent.`` I think the content is more consistent. But the style is less consistent than AdaIN that better transfers. the color tone of the oil painting and the brush textures in the lower-left case. In Fig.5, the roof color (light blue) of SANet is more consistent with the style image. In the ablation study, in Fig. 7, I think the results of one positive example has better style consistency than the results of 8 positive examples. 
+ In Table 2, this paper uses the style distance with the augmented images as metrics. However, the proposed method is the only method that explicitly optimizes this kind of metrics. The comparison is not very fair to me. 
+ The ablation study on the effect of the content contrastive loss and the feature regularization loss is suggested to also be given.


**Some small issues:**
+ What is the difference between the Wang et al. (2020) in Eq. (1) and the original style loss in Gatys et al. (2016)?
+ Some typos. ``Then, We``, ``promiseHe et al. (2020)`` and ``previous workPark & Lee (2019)`` need space. ``However, suppose`` who suppose? In Eq. (4), lambda_{s-c} should be lambda_{c-c}, later lambda_{s-s} should be lambda_{c-c}
+ Ways of some references could be improved. E.g., ``Wang et al. Wang et al. (2020) try`` can be merged as ``Wang et al. (2020) try``. ``we made a visualization for the content feature`` please explain the method for visualization. 
+ What is the backbone (AdaIN/WCT) used in ablation study?

[1] 2019 ICCV Content and Style Disentanglement for Artistic Style Transfer
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is clear and easy to understand. I believe the method is not hard to re-produce. The idea of using contrastive learning for better style feature and content feature extraction is less novel to me. The visual quality of the style transfer results is good in content preservation but less impressive in style consistency.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes to use contrastive learning to train the encoder for better style transfer and content preservation. However, the main idea of contrastive learning is not very new given the related work, and the visual results fail to convince me of the improvement of style consistency.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a style contrastive training scheme to refine the pre-trained encoder used in the existing style transfer method to make its latent space more style-consistent. It proposes an identity preserve content contrastive loss to alleviate content leak problem caused by the pre-trained encoder. It demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of our approach by adding our training scheme to some existing methods and achieve significant improvement.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. It proposes to use Gram matrix to define the style distance between images. This idea is straight and novel.

Weakness:
1. First of all, the formats of references are wrong, which makes your paper hard to read.
2. There is no explanation about the "style positive example" and "negative example" when it firstly comes out. What are the meanings of posivie and negative in this work?
3. The FIgure.2 and Figure.3 are ugly and unclear. For example, in Figure.3, there is no explation of the image pair in the left bottom. Why is there no any sampled regions?
4. The illustration of the formulations are not clear and hard to follow.
5. It lacks some details of implementaitons. For example, in Formulation.(4), it says there are corresponding loss weights for the loss terms this paper proposes. But I cannot find any statements to give the exact values of them or ablation study to analyze them.
6. There is no analysis of efficiency of the proposed training scheme.
7. There are some writing mistakes in this paper. For example, in paragraph 2, the sentence "The encoder pre-trained in different ways get different style ...". The "get" should be "gets".
8. For the userstudy, maybe the author should give the question as "chose the image with the most similar style" instead of "choose your favorite".

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors explore the irrationality of the pre-trained VGG encoder, which is a trending topic since the CVPR best paper candidate of “Rethinking and Improving the Robustness of Image Style Transfer”. The authors start by showing that some style representations generated by the pre-trained VGG are not consistent with human perception. Then, the authors accordingly propose two contrastive training schemes. Experiments validate the effectiveness of proposed method with 5 approaches to some extent.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Pros:**
+ The paper is generally well written.
+ The observation on latent space is good.

**Cons:**

*Insufficient motivation:*

- Fig. 1 and Fig. 10 are not convincing to validate the motivation of the proposed method. Only 7 pairs of results are provided, which may be easily cherry-picked. The authors are suggested to show the style distance among more images. For example, one feasible experiment would be collecting some styles with the same artwork category or from the same artists, and also those with totally distinct categories and different-aged artists. Then, the authors could put all the style images and visualize the distances between this bunch of styles in a figure with a form like clustering. In this way, it will be clear and much more convincing that subjective perception is not consistent with the style statistics. The current results in Fig. 9 are not sufficient to validate the motivation of the alignment with human perception, without showing the distances between the styles from the same category.
- Also, it is known that in the community of style transfer, there are lots of forms for style losses, like the patch-based style losses and the BN statistic matching, which is more commonly used in the literature since AdaIN. Do all those style losses fail to be consistent to the human perception, or just the Gram-based one? It will be helpful if the authors could demonstrate this point.

*Somewhat incremental method:*

- In the literature, especially in these two years, there are a bunch of style transfer methods based on contrastive learning, [a, b], just to name a few. 
[a] Domain Enhanced Arbitrary Image Style Transfer via Contrastive Learning. SIGGRAPH.
[b] Deep Translation Prior: Test-Time Training for Photorealistic Style Transfer. AAAI
It seems to me that contrastive-learning-based schemes are commonly adopted in the recent style transfer methods, which often appeared in my assigned style transfer papers in recent conferences. So, to my knowledge, such contributions by proposing novel schemes based on contrastive learning are not that strong to me.

*Experiments:*
- For the comparison with ArtFlow, the authors do not clarify which method ArtFlow is built upon, i.e., ArtFlow+AdaIN or ArtFlow+WCT. In general, ArtFlow+WCT yields more appealing results with better content preservation.
- Also, it is not convincing to claim the SOTA performance by comparing the proposed method with few methods and not comparing some recent ones. In total, there are only 5 comparative methods in the paper, where only 2 of them are published in 2021. It is a common behavior in the community of style transfer to compare with lots of methods, since it is very easy to cherry-pick some good results.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The paper is well-written.
- The proposed method is somewhat incremental.
- Details are provided to reproduce the results.
content.summary_of_the_review: My major concerns include the incremental method and the insufficient comparative experiments.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies a new way for training a stronger and more robust encoder network for style transfer. Especially, this paper firstly points out that existing encoder adopted in style transfer can not represents style feature for distance measurement.   Then this paper proposed to apply contrastive learning method to refine existing encoder. Given existing encoder as a regularizer, the perturbed style image and original different style images will feed into new refined encoder via contrastive loss.   Compared with existing encoder, the style distance among similar images are more closer in latent spaces.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper firstly points out that latent space from existing encoder in style transfer may not be the best candidate for style distance measurement. With such insights and motivations,  this paper proposed to use contrastive method for better encoder training.

However, it is not clear whether an encoder can generate with  good style transfer results must  to  generate good latent space for style distance measurement.  In general, such argument should be valid. However, given the results in Figure 6, it is become questionable. For example,  methods without proposed encoder can generate better style transfer results while the proposed method seems to have obvious artifacts. For example, the halo around the cat and  background network noise in most examples.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: It is clear that this paper is well motivated with good insights. However, it is not clear for its validation.  It is unknown that the distance difference comes from the perturbation artifacts or from style representation.  For example, the shuffled patch will generate  disconnected regions and grid noises.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper has good motivation. However, it lack of support and evidence from experiments. It is not clear that contrastive loss is a better choice to learn refined encoder  as compared with existing methods, the proposed method  can't generate visual   plausible results. Since style transfer is more quality driven application, it is hard to justify the contribution in this paper.
content.correctness: 1: The main claims of the paper are incorrect or not at all supported by theory or empirical results.
